Figure 1:Learning the task or the verifier?(a): in press_by_number, the criteriaCorigC^{\text{orig}}verify a button protocol that the instruction does not state (highlighted). Without Criteria Exposure (w/o CE) the
learner sees only whether each episode succeeded; with it (w/ CE) it also reads the criteria code, score and
stages. Right of each setting: the test successes of its library on 20 layouts, judged byCorigC^{\text{orig}}and by the
instruction-faithful criteriaCfaithC^{\text{faith}}.(b): libraries learned underCorigC^{\text{orig}}on the 16 criteria-limited
tasks, 320 test episodes each, with every episode judged by both criteria (section4.2.1). The lead of
w/ CE underCorigC^{\text{orig}}, 51.6% against 27.8%, is gone underCfaithC^{\text{faith}}(45.0% against 47.2%).

Figure 2:Overview of the self-improvement loop.Left, learning:the actor (GPT-6 Astra, high reasoning
effort) writes and executes Python cells that call the robot’s primitives on five development layouts, and sees the
result of each cell. Between batches the learner (Claude Code with Opus 5.5, high reasoning effort) turns the evidence into
one revision of the libraryℒk\mathcal{L}_{k}, whose skills are callable code that reports what it did and whose
memory entries say when to apply what, with the evidence for it; a revision is usually tried first in verification
rollouts, and the loop rolls back to the best revision so far when a batch falls clearly below it. Whether the
learner also sees the success criteria is the one switch between the two settings, w/ CE and w/o CE (the switch
under the learner).Right, evaluation:the final libraryℒK\mathcal{L}_{K}is frozen and read-only, and the same actor runs alone
on layouts the loop never saw.
